answer: Pairing a newcomer to an existing identity through a forfeitable bond blocks mass sybil growth: the sponsor stakes tokens that burn if its protege is later proven to be a clone. Sponsorship slots are scarce, so an identity's atlas of connections reflects real vouching capacity, not scripted abundance. Attackers must either corrupt enough sponsors or consume their jade reserves of capital; the basalt-hard ledger of past forfeitures is what makes each fresh clone measurably expensive.
